title: Bias-Aware Inference for Discounted Value Contrasts Combining Historical and Experimental Data
banked_reason: The fixed-K finite-multinomial LAN, Bellman delta derivative, box support-function LP, and bias-aware CI are a routine specialization of generic local-misspecification inference; no strict published-bound improvement, matched frontier, or genuinely new causal estimand is established, so tier=letter is below novelty_target=field.
gap_reasons: Yamin2026Pilot is a much closer omitted finite-pilot allocation-regret result: its Theorem 4.3 already gives inverse-pilot expected regret on an interior variance class; without a non-generic Bellman phenomenon this is tier=letter below novelty_target=field.

The fixed-K finite-multinomial LAN, Bellman delta derivative, box support-function LP, and bias-aware CI are a routine specialization of generic local-misspecification inference; no strict published-bound improvement, matched frontier, or genuinely new causal estimand is established, so tier=letter is below novelty_target=field.

The survey omits closer RL misspecification/inference comparators, notably Shi et al. (JRSSB 2022, infinite-horizon value-function inference) and Li and Yang (AISTATS 2024, locally bounded RL model misspecification), and must locate the proposed kernel against them.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery tested a comparable-source Bellman/GLS efficiency formula, then a pilot allocation and finite-pilot regret frontier, and finally a fixed-state local-misspecification sensitivity and bias-aware confidence procedure. Reviewers found the pilot regret and local-misspecification headlines subsumed by closer published theory, leaving only a letter-tier specialization below the field floor; the independent validity gate found no concrete same-topic field-tier repair. No D0 derivation or Lean formalization was reached; any future lower-tier note needs explicit intervention semantics and the missing RL comparators.
tldr: Comparable historical and experimental records can make an exact linear restriction on a discounted value contrast efficient but fragile. This project keeps the original causal contrast fixed under root-\(n\) violations, derives the two-source Bellman sensitivity operator after profiling both unknown source values, and converts statewise bounds on primitive conditional Bellman drift into an exact weighted \(\ell_1\) bias modulus. That modulus yields a feasible uniformly honest interval, an exact coverage-loss curve, and a critical radius at which unrestricted inference becomes shorter. Along an admissible statewise-box-normalized slow Markov mode with nonzero target loading, the critical primitive radius is proportional to \(1-\gamma\lambda_{\star}\); a zero-loading mode has infinite ray-specific tolerance, and an inadmissible mode yields no ray comparison.
gap: Van der Laan et al. define a projection target under value-model misspecification, Armstrong and Koles\'ar begin from a supplied approximate-moment set, Li et al. optimize historical--experimental reward-shift combinations for MSE, and Dong et al. prove safe policy improvement under local dynamics misspecification. None gives original-target confidence coverage from statewise reward-and-transition Bellman drift with two unknown source values.
fill: The project derives \(\mathcal T_B=[-B_0^{-1},B_1^{-1}]\), the exact box-constrained modulus and its dual, feasible uniform bias-aware inference, and the slow-mode threshold \(\rho_{\star}^{\mathrm{ray}}\propto1-\gamma\lambda_{\star}\) for admissible box-normalized modes with nonzero target loading, with separate zero-loading and inadmissible-ray branches.
